Context/Background: UBE2M, an essential neddylation E2 enzyme, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of various diseases, including cancers, viral infections, and obesity. However, whether UBE2M is involved in the pathogenesis of bacterial sepsis remains unclear. In an Escherichia coli (E. coli)-induced sepsis mouse model, increased UBE2M expression in macrophages in liver and lung tissues postinfection was observed. To further clarify the role of UBE2M in macrophages, mice with macrophage-specific deletion of UBE2M were constructed.
Prompt: We isolated and purified peritoneal macrophages (PMs) from control mice and mice with UBE2M deletion.  We then stimulated PMs with Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) (to mimic infection) and performed RNASeq.  Based on the differential expression analysis between PMS of control (WL) vs UBE2M deletion (KL) mice under LPS stimulation, please provide a discussion of the genes and affected pathways as relates to UBE2M deletion in the context of bacterial sepsis.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Mice with macrophage-specific deletion of the neddylation E2 enzyme UBE2M (KL) and littermate controls (WL) had their peritoneal macrophages (PMs) stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and profiled by RNA-seq (dataset: PMC11780929-count.csv). The comparison “KL vs WL under LPS” revealed marked transcriptional reprogramming: upregulation of cytokine-mediated signaling and cell-cycle programs, and downregulation of metabolic modules (notably glutathione and fatty-acid pathways). Sample sizes, sequencing depth, and replicate numbers are not specified.  

Keywords  
• neddylation  
• sepsis  
• cytokine signaling  
• cell cycle  
• metabolism  

Candidate Genes  
• UBE2M  
• IL6  
• STAT3  
• TNF  
• CUL1  

Pathway Enrichments  
Using GSEA on the KL vs WL LPS-stimulated PM contrast (run_deseq2_gsea_pipe), 62 KEGG pathways were significant (30 up, 32 down; up 48.4%, down 51.6%, ratio 0.94), 406 GO BP terms (313 up, 93 down; up 77.1%, down 22.9%, ratio 3.37), 202 Reactome pathways (91 up, 111 down; up 45.0%, down 55.0%, ratio 0.82), and 22 Hallmarks (13 up, 9 down; up 59.1%, down 40.9%, ratio 1.42).

Analysis  
Inflammatory and cytokine-mediated signaling pathways (KEGG and Hallmark NF-κB/TNF signatures) are among the strongest upregulated modules, consistent with heightened LPS responsiveness in UBE2M-deficient PMs. Cell-cycle programs (G2-M checkpoint, E2F targets, mitotic prometaphase) also score robustly, indicating proliferative or stress-driven replication signatures. Conversely, antioxidant and metabolic pathways (glutathione metabolism, biological oxidations, fatty-acid degradation, peroxisomal import) are suppressed in KL vs WL, suggesting redox imbalance upon UBE2M loss. GO terms linked to DNA replication and chromatid segregation further underscore altered proliferative control. Overall, UBE2M deletion rebalances inflammatory/amplification networks upward while dampening metabolic homeostasis.  

Targeted (Keyword-Guided) Subset  
Filtering the ORA output for TNF-related terms yields two high-confidence enrichments:  
| Gene_set               | Term                               | Adjusted P-value     | Genes (subset)                       |  
|------------------------|------------------------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|  
| MSigDB_Hallmark_2020   | TNF-alpha Signaling via NF-kB      | 2.38 × 10⁻³⁴         | IL6, NFKB1, TNFAIP3, CXCL10, IL1B…   |  
| KEGG_2021_Human        | TNF signaling pathway              | 2.14 × 10⁻¹⁰         | PIK3CD, TNFAIP3, CXCL1, IL6, FAS…    |  

These confirm that UBE2M loss amplifies a TNF/NF-κB axis in LPS-activated macrophages.

| IL6     | UP        | Pro-inflammatory cytokine; endogenous pyrogen                                                | Cytokine-cytokine receptor, Jak-STAT, TNF/NF-κB, Hallmark IR |  
| STAT3   | UP        | Transcription factor mediating cytokine/growth-factor signals                                 | Jak-STAT signaling, IL-6/JAK/STAT3, GO cytokine signaling |

| UBE2M   | DOWN      | Neddylation E2 enzyme                                                                         | not observed (absent from leading-edge lists)            |  
| TNF     | DOWN      | Pro-inflammatory cytokine belonging to TNF superfamily                                        | not observed                                             |  
| CUL1    | DOWN      | Scaffold for SCF E3 ubiquitin ligases                                                          | not observed                                             |  
| NEDD8   | DOWN      | Ubiquitin-like modifier for cullin neddylation                                                 | not observed                                             |  

Comparisons  
Inflammatory and cell-cycle signatures are concordantly upregulated across GSEA and ORA, whereas metabolic/downstream redox modules appear in GSEA down lists but less prominently in ORA—a potential artifact of ranking versus hit-list approaches.  

Implications  
UBE2M-mediated neddylation modulates both the magnitude of macrophage inflammatory responses and proliferative checkpoints in sepsis. Targeting the neddylation axis (e.g., via NEDD8-activating enzyme inhibitors) may rebalance cytokine storm and restore metabolic resilience in septic macrophages.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate top DE genes (IL6, STAT3, TNFAIP3) by qPCR or flow cytometry in KL vs WL PMs.  
2. Assess protein neddylation status and UBE2M targets under LPS stimulation by immunoblot.  
3. Perform targeted metabolomics to confirm glutathione/redox disruption in UBE2M-deficient PMs.  
4. Examine UBE2M’s role in other myeloid cells (e.g., Kupffer cells) and in vivo sepsis survival.  

Explicit Checks  
• Replication/Cell-cycle (GO_DNA replication, G2-M checkpoint): observed.  
• Stress responses (e.g., heat-shock, unfolded protein): not observed at chosen thresholds.  
• Metabolism/Mitochondria (glutathione metabolism, biological oxidations): observed.
